links.reason: Both are the madal-rider's own speech (thurai: மடல் வலித்த தலைவன்), and both cast loss as possession: the Kural's பண்டுடையேன் இன்றுடையேன் inventory against the poem's chain of தந்தது / தந்தன்றே / தந்தன்று, where மடல் is the first gift and alar, loneliness and கையறவு follow by hour. The teaches sentence names that structural difference accurately.

The two share the mullai evening (மாலை) and the absent partner, and 240 does make the evening the hour his hill மறையும். But 234's whole point is that evening is not a special hour (பகலும் மாலை துணையிலோர்க்கே), so a teaches sentence explaining 'why evening is the worst hour' sets 234 against its own claim.

20 has the sea-island campaign (இருமுந்நீர்த் துருத்தியுள் முரணியோர்த் தலைச்சென்று கடம்புமுதல் தடிந்த) and 45 the spear that drove back the sea (வேல்இடுபு ... பனிக்கடல் மறுத்திசினோரே), so the feat does grow. However 'father' and 'son' and the decade title come from the colophon, not the poems, and 45 itself still names human foes (தெவ்வர், line 15).

212 rests on the one word அறவற்கு, and 1154 imagines the assurer leaving (நீப்பின்) and asks who is at fault. Those claims are not incompatible: one is a girl's confidence and the other a hypothetical breach, so the Kural limits the trust rather than contradicting it.

The akam maxim கூற்றம் கோளுற விளியார், பிறர்கொள விளிந்தோர் (61.1-2) is the creed behind the rite in Puram 93, where a body dead by disease (நோய்ப்பால் விளிந்த யாக்கை) is cut with a sword so that it may go where heroes go (மறவர் செல்வுழிச் செல்க). Using the same creed once as a royal funeral rite and once as the reason a man leaves home is a specific shift, and the note describes both verses correctly.
links.text_issue: purananuru:93 lines 2-11 are compressed; the rite reading is likely but the syntax is not certain

links.reason: The two share a real image: a son on the father's chest spoils his finery (பட்டஞ் சிதைப்ப; அணி சிதைப்பான்). But the venba never says the crushed பட்டம் is another woman's token, and in Kali 79 the spoiled marks anger the other women; they do not expose him to the wife. So the 'exposes him' lesson reads Kali into the four lines.
links.text_issue: ainthinai_ezhupathu:45 line 2 (மேற்றுச் சிறுதாய காய்வஞ்சி போற்றுருவி) is obscure

links.reason: Both turn on the rare term கிழமை for old friendship: Puram 223 has கிழமைத் தொன்னட்புடையார, and the Kural defines பழைமை as நட்பு that does not curtail கிழமை. The stone 'giving room' (இடங் கொடுத்து அளிப்ப) to such friends who go to him is a concrete extreme of that liberty, so the pair teaches something specific.

The same sign, a bloomed konrai, gets opposite verdicts in the friend's comfort. Kuru 66 calls the trees மடவ, having taken வம்ப மாரி for கார, while Kar Narpathu 4 has காடுங் கடுக்கை ... பூத்தன as the season that is பசலை மருந்து. That is a real incompatibility about what the bloom means, and the lesson that the comfort lies in the argument and not in the flower holds.

The madal threat recurs: 58.22 has மன்றத்து மடல் ஏறி, and in 61.22 the friend quotes மடல்மா ஏறி and laughs (நாண் இலன்). But 58 already aims the threat at the girl's people (ஒறுப்பின், யான் ஒறுப்பது நுமரை), so the pair adds little to that point. The friend of 61 is a companion, not a guardian; her concern is the father's heart (எந்தை தன் உள்ளம்).

Both verses use அணங்கு of a first-seen girl. But இளையள் ஆயினும் ஆர் அணங்கினளே makes her youth a concession ('though young'), not the ground of the claim, so 'pins it on her youth' misreads ஆயினும். The 'refinement of an older certainty' story is not shown by the two verses.

The scene and its words match closely: a searching woman questions brahmins on the waste road (அந்தணிர்/அந்தணீர்) and they answer கண்டனெம்/கண்டனம். Ainkurunuru gives only the report (இன் துணை இனிதுபாராட்ட), while Kali 9 adds the sandal, pearl and lute argument and the verdict அறம் தலை பிரியா ஆறு. The growth from testimony to doctrine is visible in the Tamil, and Ainkurunuru's அறம்புரி அருமறை already seeds it.

The shared millet stubble (இருவை/இருவி) is real, and the contrast is apt: in Kuru 133 the stubble regrows (இலையொலித்து) as she survives, while in 286 it belongs to his யாணர் land as her மாமைக் கவின் is carried off. But in 286 it is the avarai on the stubble that pods (காய்த்த அவரை), not the stubble itself, and the image there is scene rather than figure, so this is same_image, not a qualification.

The Kural's point is narrow: she cannot see his fault (பழிகாணேன்) only at the moment of nearness. The Thinaimalai's object of காணேன்/காணா is unclear, and on the marker's reading it is the man himself in every phase. The teaches sentence's 'closeness and distance alike keep him out of view' therefore rests on an uncertain construal.
links.text_issue: thinaimalai_nootraimpathu:153 line 1 has a bracketed restoration (நோக்கு(எ)ன்) and the object of காணேன் is uncertain

links.reason: The parallel is close. Mullaippattu's king lies awake (கண்படை பெறாஅது) thinking of the wounded elephants and of those who fell repaying their food (சோறுவாய்த்து ஒழிந்தோர் உள்ளியும்). Nedunalvadai's king, not taking to bed at midnight (நள்ளென் யாமத்தும் பள்ளி கொள்ளான்), goes out to see the wounds (விழுப்புண் காணிய புறம்போந்து). The pair shows one care in two forms, thought in one poem and action in the other.

Natrinai 314.1-2 (முதிர்ந்தோர் இளமை அழிந்தும் எய்தார் / வாழ் நாள் வகை அளவு அறிஞரும் இல்லை) and Naladiyar 19 (யாம்இளையம் என்னாது ... நற்காய் உதிர்தலும் உண்டு) argue from the same premise to opposite objects. That is the parallel_domain the teaches sentence describes; neither verse limits the other, so QUALIFIES does not fit.

Within one decade the two wishes name successive steps: 6 has வரைக and எந்தையும் கொடுக்க, and 7 has தன்னூர்க் கொண்டனன் செல்க. Reading them in order does lay out the giving and then the bride's departure, which neither poem states alone.

The link stands only on the colophon's poet name. Kuru 53 is a friend's speech about a சூள் sworn before the சூரரமகளிர், and nothing in it says the oath is broken or ties it to the king. Puram 216 is about friendship without meeting, and no oath is mentioned. The biographical lesson ('the poet who staked his death ... knew') is built from tradition about the poems, not from the poems.

The wildcat with its young on the paalai road is a real shared image (புள்ளி வெருகு தன் குட்டிக்கு இரைபார்க்கும்; கொடிபடு வெருகின் ... பிள்ளை ... தாய்வழிப் படூஉம்). But neither poem makes it 'the household he leaves' or 'the provision he goes to win'. In Aka 297 the kitten following its mother sits nearer the girl who said வருவல் (she would come), which the teaches sentence misses.

The rare term உல்கு ties them: Kural 756 lists உல்கு பொருள் among the king's wealth, and Pattinappalai shows the men who guard the king's revenue levying உல்கு daily without shortfall (உல்குசெயக் குறைபடாது) and stamping goods with the tiger (புலிபொறித்து). A bare category beside a working institution is a specific gain.

Both wives turn the husband's bard away by pointing him to the other house: Aka 56 has 'இம்மனை அன்று; அஃது உம்மனை', and the venba has நெறிஅதுகாண் எங்கையர் இற்கு. One tells a comic incident and the other gives a bare taunt, which supports the claim that this was a set refusal move.

The sign is the same: the Kural's shoulders announce separation (தணந்தமை சால அறிவிப்ப), while the venba's shoulders have 'forgotten to waste' (வாடல் மறந்தன தோள்). But the venba's leaving is hypothetical (நீப்பினும்) and its cause is reputation (நயமுடையன் என்பதனால்), so it states a condition under which the sign fails rather than an incompatible claim.

The core is plausible: 325 says the waste does not harm him (அருஞ்சுரம் நலியாது) because he has her nature as companion (பண்புதுணைப் பெற்று), and 1201 says thinking of love brings unfailing joy (உள்ளினும் தீராப் பெருமகிழ்). But 'memory' is inferred from பண்பு துணை, and the Kural's claim is joy compared with toddy, not protection, so the fit is looser than 'puts that claim to a test'.

Both are kalavazhi, and both cast the slain as farm work: 36 has elephants falling like a field cleared of palms (பனைதடி புனத்தின் கைதடிபு), and 369 a full ploughing season (தேர்ஏராக ... வித்தி ... பைங்கூழ் ... போர்பு ... களம்). The teaches sentence correctly weighs one simile against a whole allegory, and the களம் of the thurai fits that imagery.

The same thunder gets opposite readings. In 208 the friend says the rain's voice seems to seek out the parted and bring them home (இன் துணைப் பிரிந்தோர் நாடித் தருவது போலும் இப் பெரு மழைக் குரலே). In 214 the woman, the season having come without him, hears it mock and roar at her grief (எள்ளி நகுவது போல மின்னி ஆர்ப்பது போலும் இக் கார்ப் பெயற் குரலே). The point that the meaning depends on whether the promise is still ahead or already broken is specific.

The phrase matches closely: இருமை வினையும் இல, ஏத்துமவை against the Kural's இருவினையும் சேரா ... புகழ்புரிந்தார். But the hymn's lines are a counted list (ஐந்தும், நான்கும், மூன்றும்), not an argument, so 'free because the god is beyond the three times' adds a causal link the Tamil does not make. Line 47 may also describe the feet rather than the praisers.

Both pair the royal umbrella with protection and the sceptre with aram. The hymn has அருள் குடையாக, அறம் கோலாக ... ஒரு நிழல் ஆக்கிய, and Puram 35 has அறம்புரிந் தன்ன செங்கோல் and an umbrella that is not வெயில்மறைக் but குடிமறைப்பது. The contrast holds: the king must be counselled into that meaning, while in the god it is his substance.

The two pressures match the Kural's pair exactly: the street women's அம்பல் with the finger to the nose, and the mother's cane (சிறு கோல் வலந்தனள் அன்னை அலைப்ப), against ஊரவர் கெளவை and அன்னைசொல். The poem then shows the fed love ending in departure (கொண்கனொடு செலவு அயர்ந்திசினால்). The pair says more than either verse.

Both use the same fact, that he is in her heart (உள்ளத்தார்; உள்ளத்துள் உவந்துறைவர்), but they make no incompatible claims. 1130 sets it against the town, and 1249 uses it to rebuke her roaming heart. Nothing in 1249 shows the argument 'trapping' her, and the teaches sentence is too thin to name a lesson.

The pairing is real: one recent meeting (நெருநல்; ஒருநாள்) set against gossip measured by a natural event (குயில் கௌவையில் பெரிதே; திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண்டற்று). But the 'fixed law' (the smaller the secret, the larger the event outdone) is not shown by two cases. The Kural's gossip is likened to the eclipse, not said to outdo it.
links.text_issue: ainkurunuru:369 sense flagged uncertain by marker

links.reason: The friend rests her comfort on his வஞ்சினம், with the rain as his வருகுறி, and 1154 asks who is at fault if such an assurer leaves. The Kural does name the risk the friend leaves unsaid, but 'mullai waiting rests on a man's word' is close to the shared topic.

Both use the same turn: போகிய அவட்கோ நோவேன் ... இவட்கு நோவதுவே against இறந்தது நோவேன்; நோவல். In each the mother redirects her grief: in 378 to the friend left துணையிலள், and in Aka 63 to the girl's night in the raiders' hamlet. Aka 63 is even spoken to the friend herself (மகளை! நின் தோழி), so the pairing is precise.

The garland-wound is shared: Kali 67 has நல்லார் தம் கோதையால் அலைத்த, புண், வடு, and Pari 12 has the wife's கமழ் கோதை கோலாப் புடைத்து, then மல் ஆர் அகலம் வடு அஞ்சி ending her sulk. The contrast of whose hand struck is real. But Kali 67 is not a festival scene, and the scar Pari 12 fears follows the thrown ball of coloured water (வட்டு எறிய), not only the garland blow.
links.text_issue: paripadal:12 lineation flag at line 59; who swears in 61-64 is unclear

links.reason: The match is close: முறைவேண்டுநர்க்கும் குறைவேண்டுநர்க்கும் ... இடைத்தெரிந்து உணரும் இருள்தீர் காட்சி is the positive form of the Kural's எண்பதத்தான் ஓரா முறைசெய்யா. But the idyll does not limit the Kural; it extends the duty to include giving, so the link is develops, not qualifies.

விலை ties them: Natrinai 300 has a chariot set at the gate as சிறு வளை விலை, and the Thinaimalai says even முந்நீர்ப் பொழிலும் would not be விலை, so she can only be given when the சான்றோர் are received. That answers the bride-price practice with the gift rite, and the limit fits QUALIFIES.
links.text_issue: thinaimalai_nootraimpathu:15 sense flagged uncertain by marker

links.reason: Both refuse the bard and both bring in the son, and எங்கையர் is the wife's barbed courtesy. But in the Thinaimalai the son's mud and dust (சேறாடும், நீறாடும்) is his play, not the household's grime set against decked rivals as in Natrinai 380's நெய்யும் குய்யும் ஆடி. The 'humble or proud by whom the dirt is laid on' lesson stretches the venba.
links.text_issue: thinaimalai_nootraimpathu:151 sense flagged uncertain by marker

links.reason: The verb echoes: the stranger of Aka 110 asks சிறுகுடித் தங்கின்மற்று எவனோ and is refused (இவைநுமக்கு உரிய அல்ல; 'பெயர்க'), while the friend of Kuru 345 herself asks தங்கினிர் ஆயின் தவறோ. The same neythal stay, refused at first meeting and then offered by the friend, does mark how far the love has gone.

Both are the friend speaking to the mother (அன்னாய் வாழி வேண்டு அன்னை). In 208 the eyes fill when his hill hides (மால்வரை மறைதொறு ... ஆர்ந்தன பனியே), and in 210 the sickness may abate if she climbs the boulder and looks at his flowering hill. Together they make an argument to the mother that neither makes alone.

These are adjacent பொருண்மொழிக் காஞ்சி maxims. 186 says மன்னன் உயிர்த்தே மலர்தலை உலகம், and 187 says the land is good wherever the men are good (எவ்வழி நல்லவர் ஆடவர், அவ்வழி நல்லை), naming no king. The second limits the first's claim about where a realm's good lies.

In the Kural the town raises the gossip they want (யாம்வேண்டும் கெளவை எடுக்கும்இவ் வூர்) as pressure toward marriage. In Kuru 351 the kin have declared the right (உரிமை செப்பினர் நமரே), and the friend mocks the town: இன்னும் அற்றோஇவ் வழுங்க லூரே. Showing the gossip's job done is a specific sequel.

The wording echoes: Kali 91's மாணா செயினும் ... காணின் நெகிழும் என் நெஞ்சு is the Kural's இளித்தக்க இன்னா செயினும் ... கள்ளற்றே நின் மார்பு. Kali adds the consequence for the man, பேணாய் நீ பெட்பச் செயல். That turn from confession to his licence is specific.

The image is the same and distinctive: the flood wrecking girls' sand-play while they weep (மணலின் எழுதிய பாவை சிதைத்தது என அழ; தண்புனல் வண்டல் உய்த்தென ... அழுது). Its use differs, one anonymous cry among many in the hymn and a jibe at the rival in Ainkurunuru. 'Taking' should be read as using a common scene, not as borrowing from the Paripadal.

Slipping bangles as the sign of his leaving is shared (செறிவளை நெகிழ்த்தோன்; இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை), and the Kural's தூற்றா does give the exposure sense. But 199 never says she climbs where all can see her; she asks her friend to climb the dune and gaze (காண்கம்). So 'claimed in the open' is not in the poem, and the remaining contrast is the common bangle topic.

Two claims about the demand 'give back her beauty' clash. The friend of 159 makes it while denying it is begging (நின்ஒன்று இரக்குவன் அல்லேன் தந்தனை சென்மோ கொண்டஇவள் நலனே). The heroine of 349 rejects that very proposal (கொள்வாம் என்றி தோழி) as worse than death, because it is asking back what was given to beggars (இரந்தோர் வேண்டிய கொடுத்தவை தா). The begging frame is engaged on both sides.

ullurai.anchor: யாம்ப லணிநிறக் கொழுமுகை வண்டுவாய் திறக்குந் தண்டுறை யூரன்

poems.note: Spoken by the parathai, who as an outsider may use the vehicle freely; the bee opening the fresh bud maps to the man and the young women he newly takes, and opening maps to first union.
The two arrows are an open metaphor for her eyes, set against the brothers' one arrow.
The night is likened to the god's colour, and the moon is openly a spear (வேல்போலும்) to the parted.
The town's plenty is set openly against her loneliness (ஆயினும்); it is a contrast, not a mapped scene.
The tiger is the stated reason for opening the door (அதனால்), so striking it removes the poem's argument.
The snake trembling at the thunder is a stock attribute of the thunder that she hears alone, which carries mood rather than an act.
The comparisons are to Siva and are open similes (அன்ன).
The kanthal opening is joined by போல to men who know their duty, so the comparison is open.

iraicchi.act: The stag, seeing its doe, rests with her in the thin shade of the ukaay even in the scorching waste.
iraicchi.sense: Even the beast of the waste stays by its mate in the heat, so the man should not cross that waste leaving his sweet companion (இன்றுணைப் பிரிந்தே).

poems.note: The lizard's cry is an omen (இனிய படூஉம்), not an act of a person in the situation.
Lines 2 and 3 are obscure (நரம் உன்னி, கொடியக நாட்ட), so no sense can be fixed.
The kid drinking its fill and frolicking is a scene of plenty in his land set against his hardness; it does not do an act the lovers do or should do.
The poem states the moral itself (பழகிய பகையும் பிரிவு இன்னாதே).
The parrots not coming even by forgetting (மறந்தும்) answers the plea நீ மறவல், but what their absence implies for the lovers is not fixed.

iraicchi.act: The drooping hen in the pond thinks of (உள்ளும்) her mate, the cock of the long lotus.
iraicchi.sense: As the hen longs for her cock, the girl longs for him, and his chest is her only medicine.

poems.note: Line 2 (புண்கயத்துள்ளும்) is hard to construe; the tag rests on உள்ளும் as 'thinks of'.
The tusker embracing a boulder as its mate is an act, but whose act it mirrors in the lovers' situation is not fixed.
The text is obscure; the cow's thought for its calf points to the son, and no sense for the lovers can be fixed.
The tiger hunting for its whelped mate is the path's danger in the mother's fear; no implication for the lovers follows.

ullurai.anchor: கொண்டலிற் றொலைந்த வொண்செங் காந்தள் கன்மிசைக் கவியும்

poems.note: The kanthal ruined by the east wind maps to her wasting body (stated in lines 1-3), and drooping on the rock maps to her clinging to the man called hard; the snake simile lies inside the vehicle.
நம்போல் joins the deer to the speaker openly, and the deer are the whole poem.

iraicchi.act: The swan walks in state around the lotus with its own mate, as a brahmin circles the fire with his bride on the wedding day.
iraicchi.sense: The swan keeps to its wedded mate while the man goes to other women.

poems.note: The போல் simile joins the swan to a wedding rite, not to the lovers, so the iraicchi test still applies.
